steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Since September 30, 2026 falls before DST ends in both the US (EDT, UTC-4) and Spain (CEST, UTC+2), the conversion is:

5:00 PM ET (UTC-4) = 21:00 UTC = 23:00 in Madrid (UTC+2)

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru uses UTC−5 year-round (no daylight saving time). Subtracting 5 hours from 12:00 UTC gives 07:00 on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST = UTC+2, JST (Tokyo) = UTC+9, a difference of +7 hours.

June 1, 2026, 9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = June 1, 2026, 4:00 PM JST.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest deadline is October 11, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT (UTC–7), which converts to October 12, 2026, 06:59 UTC.

Madrid observes CEST (UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), so on this date Madrid is still 2 hours ahead of UTC.

06:59 UTC + 2 hours = 08:59 on October 12, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST is UTC−8. March 3, 2026, 11:59 PM PST = March 4, 2026, 07:59 UTC.

Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) in early March 2026, since EU daylight saving time doesn't start until the last Sunday of March (March 29, 2026). So add 1 hour to UTC.

07:59 UTC + 1 hour = 08:59 on March 4, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1, so 10:00 AM CET = 09:00 UTC.
Los Angeles in February is on Pacific Standard Time (UTC−8), since daylight saving doesn't start until March.
09:00 UTC − 8 hours = 01:00 AM, same date (February 2, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9, Lima (Peru) is UTC-5, a difference of 14 hours (Lima is behind).

May 5, 2026, 8:00 AM JST − 14 hours = May 4, 2026, 6:00 PM Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Pacific Time on Oct 28, 2026 is PDT (UTC-7), since U.S. DST ends Nov 1, 2026.

11:59 PM PDT Oct 28 = 06:59 UTC Oct 29.

Madrid's DST (CEST) ends Oct 25, 2026, so by Oct 29 Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

06:59 UTC + 1:00 = 07:59 CET, Oct 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026:
- US Eastern Time is still in daylight saving (EDT, UTC-4) — DST ends Nov 1, 2026.
- Madrid is already back on standard time (CET, UTC+1) — EU DST ended Oct 25, 2026.

So the difference is 5 hours: 9:00 AM ET + 5 hours = 2:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

1. **Check CET vs CEST on Oct 27, 2026:** European DST ends the last Sunday of October. In 2026, Oct 27 is a Tuesday, and the last Sunday of October is Oct 25 — so by Oct 27, Europe has already switched back to standard time (CET, UTC+1). The "CET" label is correct (not CEST), so 18:00 CET = 17:00 UTC.

2. **Check EDT vs EST for New York:** US DST ends the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that's Nov 1. Since Oct 27 is before that, New York is still on EDT (UTC−4).

3. **Convert:** 17:00 UTC − 4 hours = 13:00 EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Determining the time zone (PT):**
- US daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday of November — November 1, 2026. So by November 2, Pacific Time is back to **PST (UTC−8)**.

**Determining Madrid's offset:**
- Spain's DST ends on the last Sunday of October — October 25, 2026. So by November 2–3, Madrid is on **CET (UTC+1)**.

**Conversion:**
- Nov 2, 2026, 23:59 PST → convert to UTC: add 8 hours → Nov 3, 2026, 07:59 UTC
- Convert UTC to Madrid time: add 1 hour → Nov 3, 2026, 08:59 CET

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline "11:59 PM PT" on March 20, 2026 falls after U.S. DST begins (March 8, 2026), so PT = PDT = UTC−7.

Converting: 2026-03-20 23:59 PDT → 2026-03-21 06:59 UTC.

Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) until EU DST starts (last Sunday of March, March 29, 2026), so on March 21 Madrid is still at UTC+1.

06:59 UTC + 1 hour = 07:59 local time on March 21, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through the time zones and DST rules:

- **CET (Central European Time)** = UTC+1. Note: EU daylight saving (CEST) doesn't start until the last Sunday in March — March 29, 2026 — so on March 25, 2026, CET is still in effect (not CEST).
- **Los Angeles** uses Pacific Time. US daylight saving (PDT, UTC−7) begins the second Sunday in March — March 8, 2026 — so by March 25, 2026, LA is already on PDT.

Time difference: CET (UTC+1) to PDT (UTC−7) = 8 hours behind.

12:00 PM CET − 8 hours = 4:00 AM PDT, same calendar day (March 25, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Midnight (12:00 AM) ET on October 12, 2026 falls during Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC−4), since DST in the US ends in November.

That moment = 04:00 UTC on October 12, 2026.

Madrid in October 2026 is still on CEST (UTC+2), since EU DST ends October 25, 2026.

04:00 UTC + 2 hours = 06:00 Madrid time, same calendar day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE = UTC-12. So the deadline (23:59 AoE, Oct 9, 2026) corresponds to UTC = Oct 10, 2026, 11:59.

Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2) since DST ends Oct 25, 2026. So add 2 hours: 11:59 UTC + 2h = 13:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Pacific Time in August (daylight saving) is UTC-7. So 12:00 PM PT = 19:00 UTC.

Madrid in August uses CEST (UTC+2). So 19:00 UTC = 21:00 CEST, same calendar day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Converting:

- IST = UTC+5:30
- Madrid in November = CET = UTC+1 (DST ends in late October)
- Difference: IST is 4.5 hours ahead of Madrid

11:59 PM IST (23:59) on Nov 10, 2026 → subtract 4h30m → 19:29 Madrid time, same date.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45, and Lima uses UTC−5. The difference is 10 hours 45 minutes (Lima is behind).

5:00 PM NPT (April 2, 2026) → convert to UTC: 17:00 − 5:45 = 11:15 UTC
Convert UTC to Lima time: 11:15 − 5:00 = 06:15 Lima time, same calendar date (April 2, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide is on ACDT (UTC+10:30) in October 2026 (DST starts Oct 4), while Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) until Oct 25. 

Oct 6, 10:00 AM ACDT = Oct 5, 23:30 UTC = Oct 6, 01:30 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

1. **Sydney time zone check (Oct 3, 2026):**
 Australian DST (AEDT, UTC+11) begins on the first Sunday of October, which in 2026 is **October 4**. Since the deadline is on **October 3**, Sydney is still on **AEST (UTC+10)**.

 So: 6:00 PM AEST on Oct 3, 2026 = **08:00 UTC** on Oct 3, 2026.

2. **Madrid time zone check (Oct 3, 2026):**
 EU DST (CEST, UTC+2) ends on the last Sunday of October — in 2026 that's **October 25**. Since Oct 3 is before that, Madrid is still on **CEST (UTC+2)**.

 Converting: 08:00 UTC + 2 hours = **10:00 local time** in Madrid, same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
